checked_sound: Exhaustively inventoried the current canonical's 19 clock fields across 71 clocks and 12 parameter fields across 53 parameters. The cycle-3 seam removal is complete; no row retains seam, and closure_manifest and population.json are non-duplicative owners of minted-row and population-row seam membership.

Tested duplicate facts in both directions. The exact-looking pre/post version pairs remain justified by inherited producer intervals, including the two Article 7(1)(e) clocks and four unchanged Union parameter pairs; deleting either version would leave its legal interval without a row.

The 18 non-identifier clock fields and 11 non-identifier parameter fields other than note have named consumers when populated: Stage C consumes timing, magnitude, bounds, windows, relations and applicability; D consumes anchor identity; E consumes owner, executor, completion and consequence; F/G carry the clock properties; source_phrase and intervals preserve fidelity and version applicability.

No surviving anchor, applies_when, completion or consequence_on_expiry was substantiated as an evidence predicate standing before a decision vested outright. Record classes identify holdable event anchors; the Article 39 accreditation-assessment exception is source-stated rather than invented proof.

The cycle-3 partial rejection of F4-05 survives re-review. Article 7(1)(e)-sub2 expressly opens "By way of derogation from point (e)", and no structured field on the two immediate-sampling rows links them to the deferral clock; deleting those two remaining one-clause notes would therefore break the human/downstream cross-clock link.

The retained notes on Article 7(1)(e)-sub2, Article 13(1), the almond exception, Article 31(9), Article 39 and the Cq boundaries carry source-stated clock interactions or genuine open terms. Their deletion would lose a relationship or unresolved boundary not otherwise carried by the same row.

The bound field earns its schema cost by preserving floors without prose parsing. resettable_period remains the only available structure carrying the Article 6(1) start, reset and survey basis together. applies_when, window, relation and executor each carry independently consumed facts and are not one-row decorative additions.

The new note and seam convention keys are human-review rules rather than dead letters: the note key supplies the admissibility test the verifier intentionally cannot decide, and the seam key prevents reintroduction of the duplicate per-row ownership removed in cycle 3.

The closure-manifest partition checks earn their verifier weight after per-row seam deletion: they ensure every clock and parameter has exactly one manifest owner, every held seam is empty and population counts agree with population.json. Removing them would permit silent unowned or multiply claimed canonical rows.
The duplicate-disposition-object check is not redundant: it enforces the deletion-test result sustained in cycle 3 and rejects indistinguishable objects without attempting semantic judgment.

Direct-ref implements_clock and restates_parameter dispositions retain an audit consumer: they identify the single canonical owner of a sibling or restated fact and prevent the cycle-3 derived-log divergence. The asserted bloat is limited to null-ref entries on provision versions that remain independently covered.

No admissible deletion was based on rarity, lack of a Puglian instance or absence of a held case. The Article 15(3), Article 39, Article 42, lifting and closed-cohort rows were tested only for duplication and consumption.

Read-only integrity comparison found 71 clocks, 53 parameters and 581 dispositions; canonical SHA-256 e1bc21e8c79b9ca48e956222dfc592bc87b68bf09d40bdfe372bca8fc5699afd matches generation-status.json, and all four existing projection hashes match disk.

The dated review returns themselves still earn retention as evidence because they preserve exact assertions and falsifiers. What should stop is further review on an unchanged ledger and the copying of each adjudication back into the sole authority as another narrative layer.
unresolved: The attached corpus names no implemented Stage C–G reader, so field-consumption conclusions are tested against the binding declared consumer contract and repository references rather than executable downstream code.

The note on B-CLK-EU-625-42-renewal-1y is redundant for the present row, but the structured schema still has no dedicated maximum-renewal-count field; whether a later Action model can enforce the one-renewal limit without consulting Stage A is outside this deletion-only facet.
